summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with cough, fever, and chills, and found to have right lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, which were later de-escalated to levofloxacin after clinical improvement. She had a history of a recent superficial PD catheter site infection, and oral clindamycin was discontinued due to antibiotic-associated diarrhea, with transition to topical gentamicin and mupirocin. Peritoneal fluid analysis showed no signs of peritonitis. A yeast infection was treated with fluconazole. The patient remained afebrile, her respiratory status stabilized, and she was discharged home on oral antibiotics with instructions for catheter site care and follow-up.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to peritoneal dialysis catheter
